newsitem.title: USA: Lehman shares shed buyout rumor gains.
newsitem.headline: Lehman shares shed buyout rumor gains.

text.p: Shares in Lehman Bros Holdings Inc fell sharply in early morning activity on Thursday, reversing gains won late Wednesday when rumors of an impending takeover of the company resurfaced.

Lehman shares fell 4-7/8 to 47-1/8 after adding nearly seven points in rumor-fueled gains on Wednesday. As in the past, Lehman was rumored to be the buyout target of a major U.S. bank, in this case Chase Manhattan Corp.
Both Chase and Lehman declined comment on the rumor.
"It looks like Chase didn't announce anything overnight," said one trader. "This rumor just keeps getting kicked around."
In May, J.P. Morgan & Co Inc was rumored to be eyeing Lehman, leading to a similar spike-and-retreat in Lehman's shares.
Despite the fact that the stories repeatedly fail to come to fruition, each instance of the rumor seems to spark Lehman shares to life.

"It doesn't surprise me, given everyone seems to be invoved in some kind of a deal lately," the trader said, adding, "oftentimes, when you hear these things over and over, eventually something seems to come of it."

Among recently announed deals in the rapidly-consolidating industry, NationsBank Corp agreed to buy Montgomery Securities, Bankers Trust New York Corp inked a deal to buy Alex. Brown Inc and BankAmerica Corp set plans to buy Robertson Stephens.
Most recently, Canadian Imperial Bank of Commerce said Tuesday it reached a deal to buy Oppenheimer & Co.
